message.text: Each reporter is resolved at the merged severity rather than the severity it reported.

evidence.snippet: The notice resolves under its own check and under the guardrail's, and the stricter result stands. It carries the guardrail match an analyser's configuration notice carries, so resolution reads `resolution.checks.guardrails` and the rule's `analyser` class. It also reads `resolution.checks.static.enola`, since every report resolves under its own check, by [the exact-rule decision](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md). So a repository cannot quieten this notice from the guardrails table while its Enola table is stricter, nor from the Enola table while its guardrails table is. The coordinator first answered that it resolve under the guardrails check alone; a round showed that broke the exact-rule decision, and the coordinator then chose both, which never lowers what blocks. Its ID is the guardrail's, which ignores the producing check, so a dismissal matches it as it would the guardrails check's. That breaks the [per-sighting decision](2026-11-07-resolution-per-sighting.md)'s premise that static and guardrail checks never share an ID. When a folder lists a Packwerk file in `policy-change-review.files`, the guardrails check reports it too, at `analyserSeverity`, and the two sightings merge. Only lens sightings are split, so each check's claim resolves at the merged severity, the higher of the two. A table that maps that severity to `silent` under one check, while blocking the lower one under the other, then resolves the finding wrongly. Example: guardrails reports P1 and Enola P2, and `static.enola` maps P1 to `silent` and P2 to `block`; the merged finding is silent where Enola's own sighting blocks. [Issue #607](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/607) proposes keeping each sighting's severity and class, which a stored shape needs. Melian's own round on the pull request found it. The policy-change floor keys on the rule and the path, so it treats both alike; a `package.yml` is not a `melian.yaml`, so no floor applies. explanation.what: Each reporter is resolved at the merged severity rather than the severity it reported.
explanation.whatToDo: Preserve each sighting's severity through merging and resolve each reporter's claim using that severity.
explanation.whyHere: Packwerk notices now share an ID with explicitly configured guardrail notices, whose default analyser severity is P1 rather than Enola's P2. Non-monotonic resolution tables can therefore silence an Enola sighting that should block.

properties.failureScenario: Configure policy-change-review.files to include packs/a/package.yml, guardrails resolution P1: silent, and static.enola resolution P1: silent and P2: block. Change packs/a/package.yml to disable dependencies. Guardrails reports P1 and Enola reports P2 with the same ID. The merged P1 finding resolves both claims at P1 and becomes silent, although Enola's P2 claim should block.
